You could check the dmesg for any errors, plus the logs in /var, some of them may hold details.

If you see an IRQ conflict, you may be fucked. Generally the way around that is to disable the other piece of hardware trying to use those resources. If it is another network card fighting over the IRQ position, go into the BIOS and see if you can turn off the network card without also disabling the wireless card.

Some BIOSes will let you disable them both on their own, but some will do both at the same time.

Beyond that, you could check to see if there is a firewall rule preventing communication on the wireless interface.
